title: Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields, Part II: Dwork switching motives
summary: This Part II of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure plans the Dwork family of hypersurfaces ∑X_i^N = N t ∏X_i and its cyclotomic eigen-local-systems, for every exponent datum: Qian's non-self-dual data and the self-dual data of Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor. It proves their rank, Katz's hypergeometric description, the complex monodromy (Picard–Lefschetz at 1, maximal unipotence at ∞, companion model), the residual monodromy SL_n, Sp_n or SU_n and the geometric irreducibility of the moduli of level structures, the Gauss-sum determinant formula and determinant matching, the p-adic Hodge theory of the fibres (consecutive Hodge–Tate weights, crystallinity, ordinarity near 0, Steinberg monodromy and ordinarity near ∞, generic crystalline ordinarity), and the switching theorems of Qian and of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne, which produce fibres with prescribed residual representations at two primes. Nothing here proves an automorphy statement; ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 and PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.5 consume these results.
readme: The definitive document is research/blueprint/readmes/PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII.md. This roadmap starts where PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure stops: the parent supplies the automorphy lifting and ordinarity machinery of Allen et al., and this Part II supplies the geometric families whose fibres are switched between two primes. Layers DM.0–DM.1 fix the linear and finite-group algebra and the Dwork pencil with its exponent data; DM.2–DM.3 construct the eigen-local-systems and Katz's hypergeometric description; DM.4–DM.5 compute the complex and residual monodromy and build the moduli of level structures; DM.6–DM.7 compute determinants, Frobenius polynomials and the p-adic Hodge theory of the fibres; DM.8 treats semistable models and ordinarity near t = ∞; DM.9 proves the switching theorems of Qian (non-self-dual), Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor (self-dual) and Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne (unitary case). Non-goals: no automorphy theorem is proved here (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2, PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.5).

stages.title: Linear algebra and finite linear groups
stages.description: Pure linear algebra and finite group theory used by the monodromy computations. **Objects.** Pseudo-reflections and transvections in GL(V) (DM.0/pseudo-reflection); finite unitary groups GU_n, U_n, SU_n of a quadratic extension of finite fields (DM.0/finite-unitary-group); Hermitian and skew-Hermitian forms (DM.0/hermitian-form). The companion matrix itself is imported from ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.2. **Theorems.** The cyclic-vector characterisation of companion matrices and the rank-one property of C(q)C(p)^{−1} − 1 (DM.0/companion-normal-form); Levelt's rigidity theorem for hypergeometric triples (DM.0/levelt-rigidity, Beukers–Heckman Theorem 3.5); absolute irreducibility of hypergeometric groups (DM.0/hypergeometric-group-irreducible, Beukers–Heckman Proposition 3.3); uniqueness of nondegenerate Hermitian forms over finite fields (DM.0/hermitian-forms-unique) and unitarity of conjugate self-dual absolutely irreducible representations (DM.0/conjugate-self-dual-is-unitary, BCGNT25 Lemma 4.3.4); normal subgroups of SL_n and SU_n over finite fields and simplicity of PSL_n, PSU_n (DM.0/special-linear-unitary-simple); Artin's non-isomorphism of simple linear groups in different characteristics (DM.0/artin-non-isomorphism); the Zalesskii–Serezhkin classification of irreducible groups generated by transvections, for n > 2 and odd characteristic (DM.0/zalesskii-serezhkin-classification); surjectivity onto a product of two groups with distinct simple quotients (DM.0/product-of-simple-images, from Mathlib's Goursat lemma).

stages.title: The Dwork pencil and its exponent data
stages.description: **Objects.** For N odd, the Dwork pencil Y: ∑X_i^N = N t ∏X_i over T_0 = ℙ¹ − ({∞} ∪ μ_N) over ℤ[1/N] (DM.1/dwork-pencil); its symmetry groups H = μ_N^N/μ_N ⊃ H_0 and the involution ς, the characters ξ ↦ ∏ξ_i^{a_i} and the isotypic idempotents (DM.1/dwork-symmetry-groups); Dwork exponent data with their index sets B (Qian's asymmetric data for n > 2 and the self-dual data of BLGHT11) (DM.1/dwork-exponent-datum); the quotient family over the thrice-punctured line T′_0 and the cover t ↦ t^N (DM.1/three-punctured-cover). **Theorems.** The auxiliary modulus N with prescribed order of l and N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1 (DM.1/auxiliary-modulus; QIAN23 Lemma 2.3, BLGHT11 Lemma 6.1); trivial multiplicative stabiliser of Qian's index set (DM.1/asymmetric-stabiliser-trivial; QIAN23 Lemma 3.1).

stages.title: Eigen-local-systems of the Dwork pencil
stages.description: **Objects.** The χ-eigensheaves V_λ, V[𝔫] and the Betti local system V_B (and V′_B on T′_0) of R^{N−2}π_* (DM.2/dwork-eigensheaves); the self-dual real forms over ℤ[1/(2N), ζ_N]^+ with their alternating pairings (DM.2/self-dual-real-forms). **Theorems.** Cohomology of the Fermat hypersurface (DM.2/fermat-hypersurface-cohomology, Deligne §7); torsion-freeness of integral cohomology of smooth hypersurfaces (DM.2/integral-cohomology-torsion-free); Poincaré duality between conjugate eigensheaves (DM.2/eigensheaf-duality); splitting of the Fermat fibre into eigenlines indexed by B (DM.2/fermat-fibre-splitting); local freeness of rank n (DM.2/eigensheaf-rank; QIAN23 Proposition 3.2, BLGHT11 Lemma 4.1).

stages.title: Katz's hypergeometric description
stages.description: **Objects.** Katz's hypergeometric sheaf E_λ = j^*(F_1 ∗_! ⋯ ∗_! F_n)[n − 1] attached to the missing characters ρ_1, …, ρ_n (DM.3/katz-hypergeometric-sheaf); the twisted local systems W_λ = V_λ ⊗ Ψ_λ^{−1} (DM.3/twisted-dwork-local-system). **Theorems.** E_λ is lisse of rank n, geometrically irreducible, pure of weight n − 1 with determinant M_λ(n(1 − n)/2), with an explicit trace formula (DM.3/hypergeometric-sheaf-properties); its local monodromy is a single unipotent Jordan block at 0, ⊕L_{ρ_i} at ∞ and a pseudo-reflection at 1 (DM.3/hypergeometric-local-monodromy); Katz's comparison of the Dwork eigensheaf with the pullback of E_λ along t ↦ t^{−N} up to a character Ψ_λ (DM.3/katz-dwork-comparison; Katz 2009 Theorem 5.3, BCGNT25 Theorem 4.2.1); Ψ_λ comes from an algebraic Hecke character of type A_0 and weight N − n − 1 (DM.3/twisting-hecke-character; BCGNT25 Lemma 4.2.4 corrected).

stages.title: Complex monodromy
stages.description: **Objects.** The monodromy representations ρ_t, ρ_{t′} and the oriented peripheral loops γ_0, γ_1, γ_∞ with γ_0γ_1γ_∞ = 1 (DM.4/dwork-monodromy-representations). **Theorems.** Monodromy at 0 has eigenvalues ζ_N^b, b ∈ B (DM.4/monodromy-at-zero); Picard–Lefschetz at 1: unipotent with (T − 1)² = 0 and rank ≤ 1 (DM.4/picard-lefschetz-at-one); unipotence at ∞ (DM.4/unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity, repairing QIAN23 Lemma 3.3(2)); the companion-matrix model and the transvection at 1 (DM.4/companion-model-of-monodromy; QIAN23 Lemma 3.4, BLGHT11 Corollary 4.4); maximally unipotent monodromy at ∞ (DM.4/maximal-unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity; QIAN23 Corollary 3.5, BLGHT11 Corollary 4.5); absolute irreducibility of the residual monodromy (DM.4/residual-monodromy-absolutely-irreducible).

stages.title: Residual monodromy and level-structure torsors
stages.description: **Objects.** The skew-Hermitian Poincaré pairing on W̄_λ in the unitary case −1 ∈ ⟨l⟩ mod N (DM.5/hermitian-poincare-pairing); the finite étale moduli T({U_i}) of level structures with prescribed determinant and pairing (DM.5/level-structure-torsor: Qian's T_W, BLGHT11's symplectic T_W with BLGGT14's correction, BCGNT25 Definition 4.4.1). **Theorems.** Residual monodromy SL_n(k(λ)) (DM.5/residual-monodromy-sl; QIAN23 Lemma 3.7), Sp_n (DM.5/residual-monodromy-sp; BLGHT11 Lemma 4.6, Corollary 4.7), SU_n in the unitary case (DM.5/residual-monodromy-su; BCGNT25 Proposition 4.4.2); the determinant is geometrically constant (DM.5/determinant-descends); the two-prime monodromy is the full product (DM.5/two-prime-product-monodromy; QIAN23 Proposition 3.8, BLGHT11 Corollary 4.8); the level-structure torsors are geometrically irreducible (DM.5/level-structure-torsor-irreducible).

stages.title: Frobenius, Gauss sums and determinants
stages.description: **Theorems.** Frobenius on the Fermat eigenlines is q^{−1}∏_j g(v, a_j + i) (DM.6/fermat-frobenius-gauss-sums); the determinant formula q^{n(N−n−2)/2}(∏_{b∈B}g(v, b))^n (DM.6/dwork-determinant-gauss-formula); descent of the Gauss product to ℚ_l(ζ_N) (or its real subfield for n = 2) (DM.6/gauss-product-descent); det V[λ] takes values in (𝔽_{l²}^×k(λ)^×)^n (DM.6/determinant-nth-power; QIAN23 Lemma 3.9); determinant matching at l and at the auxiliary prime l′ ≡ 1 mod N, with the corrected hypotheses (DM.6/determinant-matching-at-l, DM.6/determinant-matching-at-auxiliary-prime); Frobenius polynomials of good fibres are integral and independent of λ (DM.6/frobenius-polynomials-independent; BCGNT25 Proposition 4.2.5(1)). Roots of characters after totally real base change are imported from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4.

stages.title: p-adic Hodge theory and local monodromy of the fibres
stages.description: **Objects.** The twisted de Rham eigenspaces V_{dR,σ} with their Hodge filtration (DM.7/twisted-de-rham-eigenspaces). **Theorems.** Hodge grades of the Fermat eigenlines and consecutive Hodge numbers (DM.7/hodge-grades-of-fermat-eigenlines, DM.7/consecutive-hodge-numbers; QIAN23 Lemma 3.10, BLGHT11 Lemma 5.2); fibres are de Rham with labelled Hodge–Tate weights M(a), …, M(a) + n − 1, and W_{t,λ} with weights {0, …, n − 1} (DM.7/dwork-hodge-tate-weights); crystallinity, Frobenius polynomial and ordinarity criterion at good reduction (DM.7/crystalline-at-good-reduction); ordinarity near the Fermat point for l ≡ 1 mod N (DM.7/ordinary-near-fermat-point); inertia on the Fermat fibre for l ≡ −1 mod N (DM.7/fermat-fibre-inertia-at-minus-one; BCGNT25 Lemma 4.4.4, BLGHT11 Lemma 5.3(5)); single-Jordan-block (Steinberg) monodromy at places away from the coefficient prime with v(t) < 0 (DM.7/steinberg-monodromy-away-from-coefficient-prime; QIAN23 Lemma 3.12 corrected, BLGHT11 Lemma 5.1); the weakly compatible systems of fibres (DM.7/dwork-compatible-system; BCGNT25 Proposition 4.2.5); Drinfeld–Kedlaya's slope theorem (DM.7/drinfeld-kedlaya-slope-bound) and generic crystalline ordinarity (DM.7/generic-crystalline-ordinarity; BCGNT25 Proposition 4.2.6).

stages.title: Semistable models and ordinarity near infinity
stages.description: **Objects.** The H_0-equivariant semistable blowup of the reciprocal Dwork family (DM.8/dwork-semistable-blowup; QIAN21 Lemma 2.1). **Theorems.** Equivariant semistable models of fibres near ∞ after a totally ramified extension (DM.8/equivariant-semistable-model; QIAN21 Theorem 1.4/2.3); the log special fibre lifts over W[T] (DM.8/log-special-fibre-witt-lift; QIAN21 Remark 2.4); Hyodo–Kato description of D_st (DM.8/hyodo-kato-description-near-infinity); regular ordinarity near infinity for Qian's and the self-dual data, with stability under subquotients and semisimplification (DM.8/ordinary-near-infinity; QIAN23 Remark 3.13); the conditional theorem for general characters (DM.8/conditional-regular-ordinarity; QIAN21 Theorem 1.1 with corrected hypotheses).

stages.title: Switching theorems
stages.description: **Objects.** Qian's switching data: the CM field E, the determinant twists, the module W and the torsor T_W (DM.9/switching-determinant-data); the Weil-restricted torsor with local valuation conditions (DM.9/weil-restricted-local-conditions); the CM-induced seed R_CM (DM.9/cm-induced-seed). **Theorems.** Qian's switching theorem: a CM extension F′ disjoint from given fields and t ∈ T_0(F′) with prescribed residual representations at l and l′, v(t) < 0 above l and v(t) > 0 above l′ (DM.9/qian-switching-theorem); the self-dual switch used by BLGGT14 Theorem 3.1.2 and its Steinberg variants (DM.9/self-dual-switching); Kisin's local constancy and Berger's reduction theorem (DM.9/kisin-local-constancy, DM.9/berger-reduction-small-weight); local Dwork points with prescribed reductions (DM.9/bcgnt-local-dwork-points), the choice of switching primes (DM.9/bcgnt-switching-primes), and the auxiliary systems R_aux and S_UA of BCGNT25 Theorem 6.2.4 (DM.9/bcgnt-auxiliary-dwork-systems), with the rank-two case through twisted modular curves (DM.9/rank-two-auxiliary-system). No automorphy statement is proved here: the potential automorphy theorems that use these points are ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 and PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.5.
